name: FileUpload
description: A file upload drop zone with drag-and-drop support. A visually styled <label> wraps a hidden <input type='file'>. Supports accept filtering, multiple files, max file size validation, and exposes drag states via CSS modifier classes.

notes: The hidden <input type='file'> receives focus — screen readers announce it as a file upload button.
The label's for/id association means clicking or activating the visible zone opens the file dialog.
Disabled state hides the input from keyboard navigation and reduces visual opacity.
Error state (file too large or wrong type) is communicated via role='alert' on the error message element.
Focus indicator is applied to the hidden input via :focus-visible, with a visible outline on the drop zone.

accept.description: Comma-separated list of accepted file types (MIME types or extensions, e.g. 'image/*,.pdf'). Passed directly to the input's accept attribute.

multiple.description: Allows selecting multiple files at once.

maxSize.description: Maximum individual file size in bytes. Files exceeding this trigger the error state.

disabled.description: Disables the drop zone and prevents file selection.

onDrop.description: Callback fired when files are selected (via dialog or drag-and-drop) and pass validation.

labels.default: { fileSizeError: (count, limit) => `${count} file(s) exceed(s) the ${limit} limit.` }
labels.description: Override default labels for internationalisation. FileUploadLabels: { fileSizeError: (count: number, limit: string) => string }.

progressMessage.description: Text to display for upload progress (e.g. 'Uploading 3 of 5 files…'). Rendered as a role='status' element inside the drop zone.

className.description: Additional CSS class names applied to the root wrapper div.

states.hover: Dashed border using color-border-strong, muted background.
states.dragover: Solid border using color-border-focus, muted background highlight.
states.error: Solid border using color-border-danger, danger background tint.
states.disabled: Reduced opacity, cursor: not-allowed, drag events blocked.

do: Provide descriptive children content explaining accepted file types and size limits.
Show a file list after selection so users know what will be uploaded.
Use the error state with a role='alert' message to explain why files were rejected.
dont: Do not suppress the native file dialog — some users rely on it exclusively.
Do not silently reject files — always communicate why a file was not accepted.
Do not omit the accept prop if only specific file types are valid — it filters the OS file picker.
